### 1 — Scene
A mixed meat plate with a whole Asian pear: apparently a pork rib, roasted chicken, a breaded fried piece, small meat trimmings, and two browned beef or meatloaf pieces. The exact meat preparations are uncertain.

### 2 — Vessel
A round dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
The six foods listed below are visible. No separate sauce or dressing is apparent; cooking fat is included in the meat calorie estimates.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
Areas represent non-overlapping visible coverage. Heights are average heights across each food’s footprint, rather than maximum heights.

| Item | Plate area | Area × average height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Whole Asian pear | 14% | 74 × 4.5 = 333 ml | 0.90 | 300 g | 42 | 126 kcal |
| Pork rib, bone-in | 13% | 69 × 1.4 = 97 ml | 0.95 | 92 g | 250 | 230 kcal |
| Roasted chicken, bone-in, skin-on | 12% | 64 × 2.5 = 160 ml | 0.95 | 152 g | 190 | 289 kcal |
| Breaded fried chicken piece | 5% | 27 × 2.5 = 67 ml | 0.90 | 60 g | 280 | 168 kcal |
| Small browned meat trimmings | 4% | 21 × 0.9 = 19 ml | 0.95 | 18 g | 350 | 63 kcal |
| Two beef/meatloaf pieces | 8% | 42 × 1.5 = 64 ml | 0.95 | 61 g | 250 | 153 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 14 + 13 + 12 + 5 + 4 + 8 = **56% of the plate**, consistent with the exposed rim and gaps. Bone-in calorie densities are approximate averages per plated weight, including bone.

### 8 — Sanity check
The estimate is **about 780 g and 1,030 kcal**. The large whole pear contributes roughly 300 g, while the meats contribute roughly 480 g including bones. This is plausible for the visible plate, although meat identification, hidden bones, and fat content introduce substantial uncertainty.
